title: Fur, Milk and Ear Bones
question: What do a bumblebee bat and a blue whale have in common?
hook: One mammal is 30 to 40 millimetres long and another reaches 30 metres, yet both count as the same kind of animal.
idea: Mammals are defined by milk-producing glands, fur or hair, a broad neocortex and three middle ear bones, however different their bodies look.

beats.prompt: An animal has fur and feeds its young milk, yet it lays eggs. How do scientists classify it?

choices.label: Not a mammal, since every mammal gives birth to live young
choices.feedback: It tempts because nearly all mammals do, but five monotreme species are the exception.

choices.label: A mammal, one of the five egg-laying monotreme species
A bird, since birds are the animals that lay eggs
choices.feedback: Mammals are distinguished from birds by their traits, and egg-laying alone does not make an animal a bird.

beats.explain: All modern mammals give birth to live young except the five monotreme species, which lay eggs.

beats.prompt: Sort each animal into its order.
beats.explain: Rodentia holds gnawing mammals such as mice, beavers and capybaras; Carnivora includes cats, bears and seals.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it describes.
pairs: Offspring draw nutrition through a temporary organ
Make milk to feed the young
beats.explain: Each term names a feature or field tied to mammals: egg laying, the placenta, the science itself, or milk feeding.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Mammals are marked by milk glands, fur or hair, and three middle ear bones.
Those traits set mammals apart from reptiles and birds.
Mammal ancestors split from the ancestors of reptiles and birds over 300 million years ago.
So mammals must have evolved from birds once non-avian dinosaurs were gone.
beats.explain: Mammal ancestors diverged from the ancestors of reptiles and birds long before; mammals only reached their modern diversity after non-avian dinosaurs went extinct.
